rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to maximize the chance of observing all 10 compounds while revealing retention ranges and critical peak pairs. The midpoint temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how much of the current resolution margin survives. Keeping the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed isolates the effect of gradient steepness.

The 10-minute gradient eliminates the time penalty but compresses a central peak cluster. Raising temperature tests whether altered selectivity can separate that cluster while retaining the short analysis time.

Test the upper temperature limit to extend the promising selectivity change without introducing a time penalty. Monitor the entire central cluster, since improving the current closest pair may create a different critical pair.
An intermediate temperature should balance the competing central-pair separations seen at 50 and 60 °C. Keep the fast gradient unchanged to seek better resolution with no time penalty.

Slightly flatten the gradient at the best temperature to improve the newly limiting central separation. The current last-peak time leaves room for a modest increase in gradient duration without necessarily incurring a time penalty.

This preserves injection 6’s gradient slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute and temperature, so all peaks should experience the same gradient before eluting. The lower endpoint is reached after the observed last peak, making this different method a strong candidate to retain CRF 1.000.

Preserve the successful gradient slope and temperature while lowering the endpoint to 0.65. The gradient still extends beyond the last observed peak, so this method should retain the maximum CRF of 1.000.

Test a slightly shallower gradient near the maximum-score method to assess the width of the optimal region. This should improve the 1.59-resolution pair while checking whether the other critical pair and last-peak time remain within their penalty-free limits.

The maximum CRF is already achieved; test a higher starting organic fraction while preserving the successful gradient slope and temperature. This explores whether a shorter separation can retain full resolution, particularly in the two critical central pairs.

Flatten the gradient slightly to recover the central separation lost at the higher starting organic fraction. This may bring both critical pairs above R = 1.5 while keeping the last peak below approximately 8 minutes and retaining the maximum CRF.

Reduce the gradient slope slightly from 0.0667 to 0.065 organic fraction per minute to lift the R = 1.47 pair above 1.5. The predicted last-peak time remains below 8 minutes, making this a promising maximum-score method with additional resolution margin.

Test a slightly shallower slope of 0.0625 to improve the minimum resolution beyond 1.55 while checking the edge of the penalty-free time window. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this run explores whether greater separation margin can retain that score.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction paired with a shallower gradient can increase the critical-pair resolution margin while keeping the last peak near 8 minutes. This explores another potentially maximum-score region without changing temperature.

With the maximum CRF already secured, explore a substantially lower temperature for an alternative selectivity pattern rather than further narrowing the 55 °C region. The fast gradient should limit the time penalty while testing whether the central cluster separates in a different elution order.

Preserve the successful initial gradient slope but begin the final hold earlier, after the central cluster has eluted. This tests whether a lower organic endpoint can retain CRF 1.000 without delaying the last peak beyond the penalty-free window.

Flatten injection 14’s gradient to improve its limiting R = 1.19 pair while preserving the stronger separation of the other central pair. Injection 16 shows that the penalty-free window extends beyond 8 minutes, leaving room to seek a maximum-score method with greater resolution margin.

Reduce the slope to 0.046875 organic fraction per minute, aiming to raise injection 17’s limiting resolution above 1.5 while retaining its other central-pair margin. The last peak is expected near 9 minutes, testing whether this improved separation remains penalty-free.

Test a slightly shallower gradient than injection 13, aiming to retain both critical separations above 1.5 with the last peak comfortably below 9 minutes. This explores another maximum-score method with more time margin than injection 18.

Preserve injection 13’s slope of 0.0625 organic fraction per minute and temperature while extending the gradient to a higher endpoint. All peaks should elute before the programs diverge, so this distinct method should retain CRF 1.000 and minimum resolution near 1.58.

Test a slightly shallower gradient than injection 19 to map the maximum-score region. The observed trends suggest both critical pairs will remain above R = 1.5 and the last peak will elute below 9 minutes, preserving CRF 1.000.

Test whether an earlier final hold can recover injection 11’s marginal R = 1.47 separation, since that pair encounters the unchanged initial gradient and should remain a useful control. This also measures how strongly a 0.50 endpoint delays the final peak at the higher starting organic fraction.

Use a slightly shallower gradient than injection 21 with a lower endpoint, aiming to retain both critical resolutions above 1.5 and elute the last peak within the penalty-free window. Injection 22 confirms that an earlier hold does not improve peaks already eluted, so the slope change targets the central separation directly.

With CRF 1.000 already secured, test temperature sensitivity around a successful method. The shallower gradient may offset some of the central-pair compression previously seen at 60 °C, while the higher temperature should shorten retention.

This untested method has a gradient slope of 0.060, between injections 19 and 21, both of which achieved CRF 1.000. It should retain both critical resolutions above 1.5 with a last-peak time near 8.3 minutes and no time penalty.
